title: research: compute the QQ16 block rounding scale and gate invoice
body:
PR2811 takes the common rounding exponent as an input. This computes it from the complete signed owner-local block and charges the scan, including zero detection and the finite-format admissibility flag. It handles negative powers of two and the most-negative signed value without a signed-absolute-value overflow.

The emitted AND/XOR/OR/NOT circuit has exactly `w*(4q+2)-2p+sum_{i<w-p} popcount(i)+3` gates. In PR2807's 456-bit example, scanning costs `3624D+1984` gates per owner per line; combined with the unchanged pair kernels, the 336-line arithmetic subtotal is `22054368*N*D+666624*N` at lambda=1. A written all-width proof and exact source snapshots accompany the implementation.

Validation:
- Registered CPython 3.12.14 normal and optimized replay passed: 309,494 exhaustive signed-block/reserve assignments, 313 wide fixtures through 4,096 bits, and 258 complete small tensor-line compositions against an independent Fraction rounding oracle.
- Five semantic mutations, a pair-local-scale counterexample, fourteen invalid-domain controls and five CLI artifact groups pass. The original PR2811 verifier also passes.
- Metadata/source pins, committed publication bytes and diff whitespace checks pass; optimized CPython 3.14.7 replay passes.

This closes one local arithmetic input contract. Physical scan/address travel, exponent retention/cleanup, fan-out/workspace realization, wrappers/maps, recursive child admission and a complete caller/consumer bill remain open. No supplier adoption, selected frontier change, full cold replay, minimum gate count or new kappa is claimed. Family decision: narrow and stop at this scan.

Credit Nick Petalas/PR2811/2807/2771/2736, ywz65/PR2707/2540, Arham Tahir/PR2681, Ali Romman and the retained QQ16/native/geometry lineage; Ross Richardson's different floor/lifting contracts retain their credit. New work by Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0; source notices retained. Author-checked, without independent human or formal-kernel review.

Coordination: [scoped claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2727#discussioncomment-18965654). Exact base, selector nonce, revision-5 scope, final freshness and overlap limitations are in TASK.json.
